machineNote: The ND manual names the machine NORD-100. NDInsight states the same C connector is used on ND-110 and ND-120; that is not checked in an ND manual here.
title: NORD-100 bus at a card position (plug C)

conventions.active: low = true when the line is low (ND suffix 0); high = true when high (suffix 1); none = power
conventions.direction: seen from an I/O card: in, out, bidir, 'out, open collector (shared)'
conventions.confidence: read = stated in the source; inferred = worked out, the note says from what; open = not known
conventions.pins: connector C, row a/b/c, pin 1-32 (96 pins), from the backplane table

differsFromNord10: Read from both sources: the NORD-100 bus shares 24 lines between address and data (BD0-23 with BAPR/BDAP) and uses the BDRY/BINACK handshake; the NORD-10 I/O positions have separate BA0-BA17 and BD0-BD15 lines and different pin numbers. The two buses are not interchangeable.

disagreements.value: NDInsight ND-100-BUS-C-CONNECTOR.md differs from the 1980 table image in these source/used cells (image value first): a18 BINPUT used CM vs C; a19 BDRY used CI vs C; a22 INIDENT used I vs CI; a28 +12V used CI vs CMI; a30 used CM vs CMI; a32 GND used CMI vs --; b13 RESTART used C vs I; b14 RUN source C used I vs source I used C (the ND text says RUN is generated by the CPU); b19 BINACK used I vs C; b23 BMINH used CM vs CMI; b29 used CI vs CMI; b30 used CM vs CMI; c1/c2 blank vs P/CMI; c18 BDAP used MI vs CI; c20 BMEM source C used MI vs CMI/CMI; c22 OUTIDENT used I vs CI; c26 used I vs P; c27 used CMI vs CI; c28 used CI vs P; c29 used CI vs P; c30 used CM vs P. Signal names and pin positions agree everywhere.
disagreements.page: Appendix F.2 NORD-100 Backplane Table, printed page F-2, PDF page 214 (read from the page image)

electrical.value: Logical 0 = 2.4 to 5.0 V, logical 1 = 0 to 0.5 V (active low TTL); maximum load 0.8 mA per slot; receivers with hysteresis recommended on sensitive inputs.

sources.note: Secondary source. Its pin table comes from the owner's spreadsheet 'ND-120 Commands' (sheets C-BUS, C-PLUG); its driver and pull-up facts describe the ND-120 3202D CPU card. The ND original of those facts was not checked here. Where its source/used codes disagree with the 1980 table image, the image wins (see 'disagreements').
Appendix F gives the full backplane table (connector C, rows a/b/c, pins 1-32) and a definition of each signal; section I.2.3 names the plugs A, B, C.
